title: Exquisite Errors: Diagnostic Manual of Codec Orders (DMCO-I)

description.main: An inventory of more than 300 codec errors, the glitches that distort digital video, sorted into typologies on the model of the psychiatric DSM. Barry van der Rijt made the images over two years and labels each order positively rather than as a disorder.
description.extended:
A diagnostic manual for digital glitches, in which the Dutch artist Barry van der Rijt classifies codec errors the way psychiatry classifies mental disorders.

Over two years van der Rijt produced and catalogued more than 300 distorted images, each a codec order with its own entry. The classification follows the model of the DSM, with one reversal: every order is labelled positively rather than as a defect. The book has a foreword by Trudy Dehue, was designed by Rob van Hoesel and Carel Fransen, and runs to 288 pages in an Otastar softcover. The first edition was 500 copies.

Van der Rijt was diagnosed with ADHD about a decade before the book appeared, and the project treats his own diagnosis as a reason to look at deviation as something to describe rather than correct. The Eriskay Connection of Breda published it in 2015.
description.artist_bio: Barry van der Rijt is a Dutch visual artist.

notes: Also issued by the publisher in an edition with three inkjet prints; a separate set of 18 Exquisite Errors postcards has its own ISBN (9789492051110). Retailers give differing publication dates in 2015. Identified from a spine photograph; edition not checked against the copy.
